root_cause.text: In `check_swap_activate()` in `fs/f2fs/data.c`, when the first extent of a small swapfile is unaligned to section boundaries and rounding up `nr_pblocks` to `blks_per_sec` exceeds `sis->max`, the code incorrectly treats this as the last extent by setting `last_extent = true` and using `last_lblock - cur_lblock` for migration, then fails to retry mapping for subsequent extents, leaving them unmapped.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "When the first extent is unaligned and `roundup(nr_pblocks, blks_per_sec)` exceeds `sis->max`, we subtract `blks_per_sec` resulting in `nr_pblocks = 0`. The code then incorrectly assumes this is the last extent, sets `nr_pblocks = last_lblock - cur_lblock` (entire swapfile), and performs migration. After migration, it doesn't retry mapping, so subsequent extents are never processed." The patch moves `last_extent` declaration outside the loop and changes the condition to `if (!last_extent && ...)` and always goes to `goto retry` after migration, ensuring mapping is re-evaluated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a flag to identify the last extent during swap activation to fix incorrect handling of the final block extent.
intent_record.what: Added a boolean variable `last_extent` initialized to `false` before the `retry` label in the `check_swap_activate` function.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the variable `last_extent` is now available for use in subsequent code within the loop, allowing the function to track whether the current extent is the last one being processed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect handling of last extent in swap activation check by using an outer last_extent variable to skip alignment validation for the final extent.
intent_record.what: Modified the condition in check_swap_activate to check !last_extent before checking alignment/zone conditions, and removed the local declaration of last_extent inside the if block.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the not_aligned increment and associated logic are only executed when the current extent is not the last one, and the alignment/zone conditions are met; previously, last_extent was always false because it was declared locally, so the condition was effectively unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always re-lookup block mapping after block migration by removing the `last_extent` condition, fixing a potential bug where mapping was not refreshed when an extent existed.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional check `if (!last_extent)` before `goto retry;` and added a comment `/* lookup block mapping info after block migration */`.
intent_record.how: The code now unconditionally jumps to the `retry` label instead of only jumping when `last_extent` is zero. This ensures that block mapping information is always refreshed after block migration.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by fixing the incorrect handling of the last extent in swap activation, using an outer last_extent variable to skip alignment validation for the final extent, which prevents the bug where the first extent is mistakenly treated as the last and subsequent extents remain unmapped.

The group's core intent is to remove the `last_extent` condition and always re-lookup block mapping after migration, which directly fixes the vulnerability where incorrect setting of `last_extent = true` prevented retrying mapping for subsequent extents.

candidates.rationale: Rounding up nr_pblocks may cause it to exceed sis->max, leading to incorrect last extent detection and skipping retry for subsequent extents.

This condition triggers setting last_extent = true and using last_lblock - cur_lblock for migration, which incorrectly treats the first unaligned extent as the last and prevents retry for remaining extents.
When last_extent is set to true, this condition blocks the retry loop, leaving subsequent extents unmapped and causing the vulnerability.

The local declaration resets the flag each time an unaligned extent is encountered, conflicting with the global purpose of identifying the last extent and contributing to the incorrect skip of retries.

vuln_statements.explanation: When last_extent is set to true (due to rounding up nr_pblocks exceeding sis->max for an unaligned first extent), this condition blocks the retry loop that re-maps subsequent extents, leaving them unmapped and causing the vulnerability.

This condition triggers when the rounded nr_pblocks makes the current extent appear to extend beyond the maximum swapfile size, incorrectly setting last_extent = true and using last_lblock - cur_lblock for migration, thus treating the first unaligned extent as the last and preventing proper handling of subsequent extents.
Rounding up nr_pblocks to blks_per_sec may cause it to exceed sis->max, leading to the incorrect detection of the last extent and the subsequent failure to retry mapping for remaining extents.

This local declaration resets the last_extent flag at each iteration, conflicting with the intended global purpose of marking the last extent and contributing to the incorrect skip of retries when an unaligned first extent triggers the last-extent logic.
